### 3.2. Study of the truncated model
We apply the result of Lemma 3 to the study of the finite-dimensional truncated model composed of (9) and (11c).
Lemma 4. Under the assumptions of Theorem 2, there exist $\sigma, C_1, C_2, C_3, \bar{C}_4, \bar{C}_5, \bar{C}_6 > 0$ such that, for any $D \in C^1(\mathbb{R}^+, \mathbb{R})$ with $|D - D_0| \leq \delta$, $X_0 \in \mathcal{H}$, and $d_1, d_2 \in C^1(\mathbb{R}^+, \mathbb{R}^m)$, $Y$ defined by (10), where $(X, u) \in C^0(\mathbb{R}^+, \mathcal{H}) \times C^1([-D_0 - \delta, +\infty); \mathbb{R}^m)$ is the mild solution of the closed-loop system (11) associated with $(D, X_0, d_1, d_2)$, satisfies
$$
\|Y(t)\| \leq C_1 e^{-\sigma t} \|X_0\| \mathcal{H} + C_2 \sup_{\tau \in [0, t]} e^{-\sigma(t - \tau)}  \| d_1 (\tau)\|
$$
$$
+C_3 \sup_{\tau \in [0, \max(t - D_0 - \delta), 0)]} e^{-\sigma (t - \tau)} \| d_2 (\tau)\|
$$
for all $t \geq 0$. Furthermore, the control law $u$ satisfies (14) with $\kappa = \sigma$ for all $t \geq 0$.
Proof. Let $\delta \in (0, D_0)$ satisfying the small gain condition (12) be given. Let $\sigma, N > 0$ and $M \geq 1$ be the constants provided by Lemma 3 for $A = A_{\text{cl}}, C = B_{N_0} K, q = 1, r = D_0$, and $\epsilon = \delta$. We introduce the Artstein transformation [1, 31] by defining, for all $t \geq 0$,
$$
Z(t) = Y(t) + \int_{t-D_0}^t e^{(t-D_0-s)A_{N_0}} B_{N_0} u(s) \, ds. \tag{27}
$$
As $u(\tau) = 0$ for $\tau \leq 0$, we obtain that $u = \varphi K Z + \varphi d_2$. Taking the time derivative, (9) yields for all $t \geq 0$
$$
\dot{Z}(t) = \left\{ A_{N_0} + \varphi e^{-D_0 A_{N_0}} B_{N_0} K \right\} Z(t)
$$
$$
+ B_{N_0} K \left\{ \left\lbrace \varphi Z (t - D(t)) - \varphi Z (t - D_0) \right\rbrace \right\}
$$
$$
+ B_{N_0} d_1 (t) + \varphi (t) e^{-D_0 A_{N_0}} B_{N_0} d_2 (t)
$$
$$
+ B_{N_0} \left\lbrace \left\{ \left\lbrace \varphi d_2 (t - D(t)) - \left\lbrace \varphi d_2 (t - D_0) \right\rbrace \right\} \right\rbrace
$$
We first study the case $t \geq t_1 \triangleq t_0 + D_0 + \delta$. We have for all $t \geq t_1$ that $\varphi (t) = \varphi (t - D_0) = \varphi (t - D(t)) = 1$ and thus
$$
\bar{Z}(t) = A_{\text{cl}} Z(t) + B_{N_0} K \left\lbrace Z(t - D(t)) - Z(t - D_0) \right\rbrace
$$
$$
+ B_{N_0} d_1 (t) + e^{-D_0 A_{N_0}} B_{N_0} d_2 (t)
$$
$$
+ B_{N_0} \left\lbrace d_2 (t - D(t)) - d_2 (t - D_0) \right\rbrace.
$$
Consequently, by applying Lem. 3 to the above ODE with $x(t) = Z(t + t_1)$, it follows from (17) that, for all $t \geq t_1$,
$$
\|\bar{Z}(t)\|
$$
$$
\leq M e^{-\sigma(t-t_1)} \sup_{\tau \in [t_0, t_1]} \| Z(\tau) \| + \bar{N}_1 \sup_{\tau \in [t_1, t]} e^{-\sigma(t-\tau)} \|d_1(\tau)
$$
$$

### 4. Exponential ISS of the infinite-dimensional system

This section is devoted to the proof of the main result of this paper: namely, Theorem 2. Let \( \sigma > 0 \) be provided by Lemma 4. Let \( 0 < \kappa < \min(\alpha , \sigma) \) be given and define \( \varepsilon = \kappa / \alpha \in (0, 1) \). First, we infer from \( g = \sup_{n \geq N_{0}+1} \left| \frac{\lambda_{n}}{\operatorname{Re} \lambda_{n}} \right| < \infty \) that the following estimate holds true for all \( n \geq N_{0}+1 \)

\[
\Vert {\Re \lambda_{n} \vert} = \left| \frac{\lambda_{n}}{\operatorname{Re} \lambda_{n}} \right| \times \left| \frac{\operatorname{Re} \lambda_{n}}{\operatorname{Re} \lambda_{n} + \kappa} \right| \\
\leq g \left| \frac{-\alpha}{\alpha + \kappa} \right| \leq \frac{q g_{n}}{\alpha - \kappa},
\]

where we have used the facts that \( \operatorname{Re} \lambda_{n} \leq q - q = \alpha - \kappa \leq 0 \) and the function \( x \to x / (x + \kappa) \) is positive and strictly increasing for \( x \in (-\infty , - \kappa ) \). Now, from the integral expression (7) of the coefficient of projection \( c_{n} \) and using the definition of the boundary input (4), we have for all \( t \geq 0 \)

\[

\]

We now evaluate the different terms on the right hand side of (34). Denoting by \( e_{n}, e_{2}, \cdots, e_{m} \) the canonical basis of \( K^{m} \), we have \( d_{1}(t) = \sum_{k=1}^{m} d_{1,k}(t) e_{k} \) with \( d_{1,k}(t) \in K \). 本节将通过延迟两个系统到达 \( Z\in C^1([0,N_{D}-\delta],\mathbb{K}^N) \) 和 \( Z\in C^1([0,N_{D}-\delta],\mathbb{K}^{M}) \)；其中 \( D\in C^1([0,T];\mathbb{K}^2) \) 具有 \( T \) 和 \( X \部倒边模型；在 \( [0,N_{D}-\delta] \)） 也可见 (A4), 接下来，我们设计一个传输链路模型，仅当时间延迟 \( \tau < N_{D}-\delta \) 且 \( X=Z \) 时一次。我们必须实现一个分配执行系统的更改，即从系统 \( [0] \) 调到 \( [N_{D}-\delta] \) 时需要交替选择滤波器并清除所有可能被丢弃的误差。我们维护一个两个系统过滤器。一旦两个系统完成 (在 \( [0,\tau_{0}] \))，假设过滤器准确无错误，示例：连续交替频谱\((C^{0},C^{1},...,\cdot,0)\) 完成后，有两个接收滤波器 \( \tilde{X}(t), \tilde{Z}(t) \) 输出；这两个滤波器 \( \tilde{X}, \tilde{Z} \) 下放置两个离散映射运算符 \( \chi,\mu \)。我们将系统应用于系数 \( c(t) \)、观察 \( B_0,\tilde{B_0} \) 并与位置 \( t_0 \) 的离散操作，同时定义 \( \eta\in C^1([0,T];\mathbb{K}_0) \) 和 \( \eta_H\in C^0([0,\tau-\delta];\mathbb{K}^0) \) 瞬时系统延迟。来自模型，电子信号包含一个只包含从 \( c(t) \) 到 \( d(t) \) 的信号，参考 \( c^0(c_1(\bar{d})-d_{0}-\delta),q <k<1\) 为三角矩阵 \(\tilde{A}(\tau)=\bar{B}(c_1(\bar{c_0}4_{D},b_{0})\cdot c_{1}(\bar{c_0})
